svg.title: Kaplan and Chinchilla as two slopes on log-log axes
svg.desc: Optimal parameter count against training compute, both axes logarithmic with decade ticks and no absolute values. Two straight lines leave a common anchor on the left: the steeper one is Kaplan 2020, where parameters scale as compute to the power 0.73, and the shallower one is Chinchilla 2022, where parameters scale as compute to the power 0.50 and tokens take the other half. Because a power law is a straight line on log-log axes, the disagreement is a difference of slope, so the two prescriptions agree near the anchor and diverge as compute grows. At one budget the gap is labelled with the measured case: Gopher at 280 billion parameters and 300 billion tokens against Chinchilla at 70 billion parameters and 1.4 trillion tokens, a model four times smaller that won. The figure is schematic; the slopes are the fitted exponents but the axes are not calibrated.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: One exponent apart: why Kaplan and Chinchilla diverge
